subject: RAG evaluation playbook, retriever/reranker choices, and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@hightidehealth.com>, Tom Brenner <tbrenner@hightidehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: RAG eval playbook + recommended next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to meet the Hightide team. Quick recap and a concrete proposal for the RAG evaluation so we can align on scope and next steps.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: accurate, auditable answers for clinician-facing FAQ and care-path guidance. High priority on factual grounding and minimizing hallucinations; latency preference under 300ms P95 for short replies.
- Data: ~1200 policy & protocol docs (PDFs + a Confluence dump), lots of short tables and some scanned pages.
- Success metrics: grounding rate (percentage of answers citing a retrieved doc), top-1 retrieval hit-rate for gold references, hallucination rate <= 2% on sample eval set.

Redwood recommended evaluation plan (high level)
1) Retriever experiment matrix
   - Sparse (BM25) baseline vs dense (FAISS/HNSW on cached embeddings).
   - Chunking: 512-token and 2048-token experiments (we expect different recall tradeoffs due to long tables).
   - Pre-filtering: metadata filter on "document_type" (policy vs chart) to reduce noise.

2) Reranker options
   - No reranker (generation uses retrieved set as-is) — fast, cheaper, likely lower fidelity.
   - Bi-encoder reranker (lightweight re-score) — good throughput, moderate quality uplift.
   - Cross-encoder / cross-attention reranker (highest quality, higher latency) — use for top-k re-ranking (k=10 -> 1) in canary runs.

3) Model / quantization recommendations
   - For high-quality canary: Llama-2-13B-QLoRA or Mistral-small quantized (8-bit) as middleware model with cross-encoder rerank.
   - For latency-sensitive baseline: 7B quantized generator + bi-encoder reranker.

4) Grounding and quality metrics to collect
   - Retrieval hit-rate @1/@5, grounding-rate (explicit citation in generation), hallucination rate (manual eval on 300 samples), P50/P95 latency, tokens/response cost.

5) Evaluation artifacts we need from you
   - Representative query set (we sketched 300 sample queries in the call) — please see attached hightide_sample_queries.csv.
   - Document inventory/export (Confluence export or shared Drive) — you mentioned getting that to us by end of week.

Proposed next steps and timeline
- You: share content inventory + any redaction constraints (by EOW 11/7).
- We: kick off a retrieval baseline + reranker ablation and deliver benchmark results and a short playbook (7 business days after data access).
- Joint review: 30–45 minute review of results, determine pilot configuration and canary rollout plan.

Questions / open items
- Are there strict PII or retention restrictions beyond standard health data rules?
- Any internal preference for vector store (you mentioned an internal ES cluster) or ok for us to host a short-term FAISS snapshot?

Attachments: hightide_sample_queries.csv (sample queries we discussed).

Thanks — happy to adjust based on priorities.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: RAG eval playbook + recommended next steps

Jonas — thanks for the tidy recap, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side before we hand over data: 

1) Reranker latency/cost: can you quantify the expected delta between bi-encoder and cross-encoder for our target P95? We're worried about any approach that will push us over 300ms for short answers.
2) Models: you mentioned Llama-2-13B-QLoRA — do you have a smaller/compressed fallback that preserves grounding quality? Our infra budget will likely prefer 8–13B-sized models.
3) Data delivery: attaching the content_inventory.csv that shows doc counts and file types — you'll notice ~200 scanned PDFs (OCR available). Any special handling for scanned/ocr content?

Timeline: procurement wants a quote and a one-page test plan to justify POC spend by 11/10. Can Redwood provide that? Also please include any additional data security steps we should list for our security review.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Dir. Product — Knowledge Systems
Hightide Health
attachment: content_inventory.csv


From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@hightidehealth.com>, Tom Brenner <tbrenner@hightidehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: RAG eval playbook + recommended next steps

Priya — great questions. Answers inline and next steps.

1) Reranker latency/cost
   - Bi-encoder: adds ~8–20ms per candidate on our hosts; if you run a bi-encoder on top-k=50 it’s ~120–250ms extra (depends on hardware).
   - Cross-encoder: re-ranking k=10 with a 13B cross-encoder typically adds ~160–350ms. Practically we do a hybrid: bi-encoder to cut to top-50, cross-encoder on top-10 for production canary. That pattern usually keeps P95 in your 200–350ms range depending on host.

2) Smaller/compressed fallback
   - Yes — 7B quantized variants (7B QLoRA or 7B FP16) provide a good latency/cost tradeoff. Our recommendation: canary with 13B (best quality) + fallback to 7B quantized with simpler reranker if latency or cost thresholds are breached.

3) Scanned PDFs / OCR
   - We’ll ingest OCR text as separate doc fields and mark OCR confidence. For low-confidence pages we run a stricter retrieval filter and surface the source with a low-confidence flag.

Procurement / security notes (short bullets you can copy into the one-pager)
- Data: Redwood can operate on a short-term hosted FAISS snapshot or we can run the eval inside your VPC (private deployment).
- Security: SOC 2 controls, optional customer-managed KMS, and audit logs for retrieval traces and inference requests.
- Cost: rough POC estimate (7 business-day benchmark + 2-week pilot) — USD 12k–18k depending on chosen model footprint. We’ll convert this to a formal quote once scope is finalized.

I’ve started a quick benchmark run against the queries you sent; results so far are preliminary — see link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-hightide-rag-benchmarks and attached benchmark_results_v1.xlsx for the initial metrics (retrieval @1/@5, latency, sample hallucination counts). Also attached eval_run_config.json (the run config we used).

If that looks reasonable, can we set a 30-minute alignment call on Thursday 11/6 to review the benchmark and lock the POC test plan?

Best,
Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
Attachments: benchmark_results_v1.xlsx, eval_run_config.json


From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Tom Brenner <tbrenner@hightidehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: RAG eval playbook + recommended next steps

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the quick benchmark and clarity. A couple internal notes and a small ask for the POC design: 

- Canary rollout suggestion: start with hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense overlay) -> bi-encoder rerank -> cross-encoder only for escalations or low-confidence responses. Include a seamless fallback to the 7B quantized path for latency spikes.
- Eval: add an ablation that measures cross-encoder benefit on "long-table" queries separately — early signals show tables are where dense retrieval helps most.
- Prompts & seed set: please include the exact prompt templates and 20 seed prompts we used in the call as part of the deliverable; we need them to reproduce quality regression checks.

Markus — approve moving procurement conversation to legal early; we'll prepare a short SOW and a two-month pilot price. Priya / Tom — happy to jump on the 11/6 call if that still works; will share a draft one-pager for procurement by EOD tomorrow.

—Monica
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
